newsitem.title: NEW ZEALANd: New Zealand shares close mixed on light turnover.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand shares close mixed on light turnover.

text.p: * NZ shares soft again, volume very light
* Telecom recovers, Fletcher stocks firm, Carter Holt weak
342 -4 * Volume NZ$38 million. June futures -5 at 1,105
New Zealand shares closed slightly weaker but off their lows on Wednesday as offshore investors stayed on the sidelines and turnover remained light.

The NZSE-40 capital index closed 2.60 points weaker at 2,214.46, with market leader Telecom recovering two cents to $6.37. The company said it bought back a further 418,500 shares between $6.31 and $6.37. Off market it bought 9.4 million at between $6.27 and $6.72.
Rumours persisted that Qantas was about to sell its 19.4 stake in Air NZ, but the "B" shares, of which Qantas holds about 100 million, firmed five cents to $3.95.

Brokers said a deal by Qantas, if confirmed, would remove the overhang in the stock and benefit both Air NZ and Brierley Investments, which owns 42 percent of the carrier. BIL firmed a cent to $1.34 on turnover of 2.25 million shares.

Carter Holt Harvey fell seven cents to $3.03 on continuing concerns about low pulp prices, and Luke Koekoek at J.B. Were said there were signs of some reweighting within the sector, as Fletcher Paper firmed four to $2.87.
Comments by Reserve Bank Governor Don Brash that the New Zealand dollar appeared somewhat overvalued had little impact.
"The market has no real driver to drive it positively," said David Price at First NZ Capital, while noting it had held up reasonably well in the face of weakness offshore.
He said many stocks were "neglected" in the current thin market. An example was Fernz, down 14 cents to $4.66 on volume of just 41,693 shares.
